title: Spin-Orbital Hall Nano-Oscillators using PtCr/NiFe
authors: Utkarsh Shashank, Akash Kumar, Daegeun Jo, Thi Ngoc Anh Nguyen, Jong-Guk Choi, Sambit Ghosh, Michal Strach, Lunjie Zeng, Andrew B. Yankovich, Roman Khymyn, Ahmad A. Awad, Eva Olsson, Peter M. Oppeneer, Johan Åkerman
abstract: The orbital Hall effect provides a promising route for generating angular-momentum currents beyond conventional spin Hall physics. PtCr alloys exhibit unusually large current-induced torques, but the contribution of orbital transport and the ability of these torques to sustain coherent nonlinear magnetization dynamics remain unresolved. Here we demonstrate spin-orbital Hall nano-oscillators by exploiting a homogeneous heavy-metal/light-metal alloy in which orbital Hall currents generated by Cr are converted by Pt into spin currents, producing giant spin-orbit torques. Using PtCr/NiFe heterostructures, the effective torque efficiency increases from ~0.14 in Pt/NiFe to ~0.40 in Pt0.38Cr0.62/NiFe despite substantial Pt dilution, enabling coherent auto-oscillations with the threshold current density reduced from ~ 1.07 x 10^12 to ~ 4.4 x 10^11 A m^-2. First-principles calculations show that Cr alloying suppresses the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity while enhancing the orbital Hall conductivity, and reproduce the observed torque enhancement only when orbital transport is included. Our combined experimental and first-principles results show that alloy engineering enables giant spin-orbit torques through an intrinsic orbital-mediated contribution, enabling coherent auto-oscillations without engineered multilayers and establishing a scalable materials platform for low-power nonlinear spintronic and orbitronic devices.
summary: This work demonstrates how engineering PtCr alloys into heterostructures with ferromagnets enables giant spin-orbit torques by exploiting orbital Hall effects alongside conventional spin Hall effects. By achieving a higher torque efficiency, the authors significantly lower the current required to sustain coherent auto-oscillations, proposing a scalable platform for next-generation orbitronic devices.
main_problem: The research aims to develop efficient methods for generating current-induced torques beyond conventional Spin Hall Effect physics by utilizing the Orbital Hall Effect (OHE) to create spin-orbital torque nano-oscillators (SOHNOs).
main_result: Cr alloying in PtCr/NiFe heterostructures enhances the effective torque efficiency and reduces the threshold current density for auto-oscillations, establishing a scalable platform for low-power spintronic devices.
method: The study combines experimental measurements (ST-FMR and auto-oscillation) with first-principles calculations to model the spin-orbital angular momentum transfer mechanism.
model_or_system: The physical system is the PtCr/NiFe heterostructure, where charge current generates both conventional spin currents (via SHE in Pt) and orbital currents (via OHE in Cr). Strong Spin-Orbit Coupling mediates the conversion of these orbital currents into effective damping-like torques on the ferromagnet.
key_observables: Effective torque efficiency ($	heta_{eff}$), auto-oscillation threshold current density ($J_{th}$), and magnetic linewidth modulation ($\delta(\mu_0\Delta H)$).
important_parameters: Cr concentration ($x$), which controls the enhancement of $	heta_{eff}$ (from 0.14 to ~0.40) and the reduction in $J_{th}$.
main_assumptions: The enhanced torque is attributed to an intrinsic orbital-mediated contribution, which is confirmed by theoretical calculations that include OHE pathways.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate TEM/STEM-EDXS confirming homogeneous alloying; schematics detail the spin-orbital angular momentum transfer mechanism; and spectra show linewidth modulation vs. bias current and auto-oscillation onset vs. current density.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the need for OHE over SHE, detailing the PtCr/NiFe platform, presenting experimental measurements (ST-FMR/auto-oscillations) showing performance enhancement with Cr doping, and finally providing first-principles calculations to theoretically confirm the orbital-mediated torque enhancement.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the study of current-induced torques and nonlinear dynamics in nanoscale devices touches upon non-equilibrium quantum transport phenomena that are relevant for understanding dissipation mechanisms in open quantum systems.
